svg.title: Fixed-size chunking vs structure-aware chunking with context
svg.desc: The same policy section is chunked two ways. The source section has the heading 3.2 Prior authorization under the Gold plan, a paragraph, and a small table listing drug X as requiring prior authorization and drug Y as not. On the left, a fixed 200-token splitter cuts the table in half: chunk 2 contains only the row "Drug X: PA required: Yes" without the heading, so a retriever cannot tell which plan or section it belongs to, and chunk 3 starts mid-row. On the right, a structure-aware splitter keeps the paragraph and the whole table as separate chunks along heading boundaries, and prefixes each chunk with its context, "Gold plan, section 3.2 Prior authorization", before embedding. Simplified: real chunks are longer.
svg.text: Source: Gold plan formulary › 3.2 Prior authorization (a paragraph, then a table)
## 3.2 Prior authorization. Some drugs on the
Gold plan need approval before dispensing …
| Drug X | PA required: Yes | Form PA-2291 |
✗ Chunk 2 has no heading: which plan? which section?
✗ Table row split across chunks 2 and 3
✗ Unrelated text mixed in: noisy embedding
Some drugs on the Gold plan need approval
| Drug X | PA required: Yes | Form PA-2291 |
✓ Split on headings, never inside a table row
✓ Context prefix travels with the chunk
The retriever only ever sees one chunk at a time. If the chunk does not say what it is about,
no embedding model can recover it. Contextual Retrieval automates the prefix with an LLM.
